results.summary_before: This project implements a state machine whose transition table is stored in an external SPI flash device, with inputs and current state shifted out to look up the next state and outputs. It uses a clock, reset, data in, and four general inputs, and drives chip select, data out, and five general outputs. Testing requires connecting a SPI flash device that supports the 0x03 read command with 24-bit addressing and is preloaded with state machine values. The design is notable for offloading state machine storage to external flash, but the documentation gives no details on the state encoding or flash contents.

results.summary_before: This design adds two 8-bit floating point numbers, each with a 1-bit sign, 4-bit exponent and 3-bit mantissa, taking one operand from the input pins and the other from the bidirectional pins. The result, including rounding and infinity handling, appears on the output pins every clock cycle. A silicon test report notes that the adder works well for most values but produces incorrect results for some small values, and a linked script tests all possible input combinations. It is a compact arithmetic building block rather than a complete calculator.

results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design implements a UART transceiver with both transmit and receive functions at 9600 baud, using oversampling to sample the middle of each bit period. The receiver waits for a start bit, samples eight data bits and a stop bit, and asserts a data-ready signal; the transmitter sends a byte with correct timing when a data-ready input is set. The eight output pins double as 7-segment display segments and as the UART transmit data output, while bidirectional pins carry received data and a finished-read flag. Testing requires setting the data bits and data-ready input and observing the transmitted sequence on the tx output.

results.summary_before: This design generates pseudo-random bit streams whose probability of a one equals the product of two 2-bit input vectors, implementing stochastic multiplication based on a published PN-sequence method. It is used by setting inputs A and B, applying a clock, and toggling reset low to start the PRBS generators, with outputs providing the product stream and individual operand streams. No external hardware is strictly required, though some outputs are also mapped to 7-segment segments. The documentation is brief and cites the underlying paper, but does not describe the internal implementation or provide silicon test results.
